System

Layered sprites, facing, appearance and remote avatars

Render one 2D body and compatible clothing/weapon layers while a full-height capsule moves on a 3D floor. Presentation selects poses from server-observed action facts; it cannot decide hits, gathering rewards or whether movement is legal.

Scope and player interaction

Render one 2D body and compatible clothing/weapon layers while a full-height capsule moves on a 3D floor. Presentation selects poses from server-observed action facts; it cannot decide hits, gathering rewards or whether movement is legal.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase01committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Unbound → ResolvingCatalog → Ready → FallbackVisual → MissingBody → HiddenForTransfer

WBP_Portrait observes results from URPGPaperDollComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_AnimationSet_Common. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
PresentationState: ActionTag, Facing4, ActionSequenceId, AcceptedStartServerSeconds and variant; replicated compactly
AppearanceIds: body/hair/palette/outfit/gear visual IDs; persist IDs, not component pointers
AnimationKey: body compatibility version + page + action + facing + variant
LayerBindings: body, behind, outfit, cloak, face, hair, hat, main tool, offhand, special overlay; only instantiate supported layers
FootPivotPixels: source-verified coordinates; currently unknown until the archive is inspected
VisualScale: one shared pixels-per-unit choice; do not stretch each wearable separately

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGPaperDollComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_PortraitLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
ApplyAppearanceSnapshot(AppearanceIds, Revision) -> Applied|MissingVisual; project custom client function
ResolveAnimation(ActionTag, Facing4, EquipmentVisualIds) -> MatchedSet|Fallback; project custom pure lookup
ApplyPresentationState(State) -> Updated|StaleSequence; project custom presentation command
ClearVisualBindings() -> Cleared; unsubscribe and release soft references on teardown

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Owning movement/combat/gather components publish a semantic action and accepted timestamp; the server does not send each PNG frame.
  2. URPGPaperDollComponent resolves matching body and gear pages before starting playback. Missing gear may hide that layer but cannot alter equipped stats.
  3. A single PaperZD animation driver selects the body sequence. The project adapter reads its effective frame/normalized time and drives compatible overlays from that same clock.
  4. Facing is derived from movement or action aim in the camera-ground basis with hysteresis; use a four-direction lookup, not diagonal art invented by mirroring.
  5. Remote clients use replicated action sequence/timestamp plus interpolated movement. Late packets skip to the current pose or finish harmlessly; they do not replay gameplay.
  6. On a camera elevation/floor change, keep the capsule and foot anchor in world space. Nameplates and portraits use safe identity/appearance snapshots, never account IDs.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. In L_ArtLab place a flat floor, ramp, stair, raised bridge, low wall and overlapping avatar pair; label near/far paths so occlusion errors are observable.
  2. Create ARPGPlayerCharacter from ACharacter and BP_PlayerCharacter as its child after native compilation. Add one noncolliding Paper2D body FlipbookComponent under VisualRoot; keep Capsule and CharacterMovement as collision/movement owners.
  3. Add the project PaperZD adapter and URPGPaperDollComponent. Inspect installed PaperZD source to bind its Animation Component/render component; exact plugin property names are not verified here. Do not add a skeletal montage requirement.
  4. Author DA_AnimationSet_Common mappings only for source-verified sheet/action/facing combinations. Until audit, use developer-created debug pose assets with an obvious development label.
  5. Give all layers identical canvas/pivot/scale. Test masked and translucent materials separately; small ordered layer offsets must not let a cloak sort in front of an unrelated nearer actor.
  6. Reopen BP_PlayerCharacter after each new action phase to add only that action's mapping; reopen WBP_Portrait to use the same IDs and fallback logic.

Reopen Phase01 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_ArtLab / Avatar_A / Avatar_B / OutfitProbe. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Outfit page p1 assigned during a pBOW action -> PageMismatch warning and explicit fallback; no shifted limbs.
Body clip missing -> MissingBody diagnostic silhouette; gameplay remains functional in a development lab.
Missing animation notify -> accepted hit/reward and action completion still occur from the authority.
Duplicate action sequence -> no duplicate sound or visual spawn; stale appearance revision ignored.
Two avatars cross a bridge at different heights -> world occlusion and foot alignment remain plausible; record failing material/projection combinations.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Four facings first. Proposed hysteresis 8° around facing boundaries; shared visual playback timing comes from the actual source guide when available. Eight-direction, swim, cast, dodge and mounted art remain unverified.

Diagnostics show resolved action/page/facing/body/layers and fallback reason. Emote captions and telegraphs never rely only on color. Pixel art imports and legal restrictions are detailed in the art chapters.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
